name: Type I information
statement: Control of sums with one short or structurally simple coefficient variable, typically sum_m alpha_m sum_n beta_n over mn in a target set.
pvg_translation: multiplicative splitting nu(mn)=nu(m)+nu(n) with one factor profile constrained
claim_ceiling: Type I control alone is not a prime-producing theorem.

name: Type II information
statement: Control of genuinely bilinear sums with both variables in intermediate ranges.
pvg_translation: correlation of two valuation-profile populations whose vector sum lies in the target region
claim_ceiling: A finite bilinear decomposition does not establish uniform analytic cancellation.

name: Finite bilinear product decomposition
statement: For finite coefficient arrays, sum_n c_n with c_n=sum_{mn=n} alpha_m beta_n is exactly a sum over factor pairs.
pvg_translation: sum over u+v=w in valuation space
claim_ceiling: Exact factor-pair bookkeeping does not supply estimates.

name: Level of distribution
statement: A sequence has level D only relative to a stated main term, modulus family, remainder norm, and uniformity range.
pvg_translation: aggregate residue-channel control after information-losing pushforward
claim_ceiling: Level of distribution does not by itself imply primes or bypass parity.

name: Type I/II to distribution transfer
statement: A valid transfer requires a named decomposition identity, coefficient norms, variable ranges, modulus range, and aggregate remainder estimate.
pvg_translation: profile-splitting estimates transferred to residue-channel aggregates
claim_ceiling: No transfer is licensed when any range or norm is omitted.

name: Vaughan-style identity interface
statement: Prime-weighted sums may be decomposed into structured Type I and Type II pieces using an external combinatorial identity.
pvg_translation: partition of prime-power-axis weights into factor-profile regimes
claim_ceiling: The identity is not reproved in this unit and no new prime estimate is claimed.

name: Harman sieve interface
statement: Reuse Harman ledger Type I/II and bilinear diagnostic tools rather than defining a parallel sieve system.

name: Montgomery distribution interface
statement: Reuse Montgomery distribution and large-sieve layers for analytic cancellation dependencies.
claim_ceiling: No theorem imported without its original hypotheses.

name: Aggregation loss after bilinear pushforward
statement: Residue aggregates may lose factor pairing, phase, sign, ordering, and individual valuation profiles.
claim_ceiling: Aggregate control cannot be inverted without extra structure.

name: Reject finite bilinear success implies asymptotic Type II
statement: Cancellation in a finite sample cannot certify a uniform Type II estimate.

name: Reject level of distribution implies prime production
statement: A distribution certificate for divisibility or residue aggregates is not a prime-producing certificate.

name: Parity and target-purity boundary
statement: Type I/II information can improve distribution control while still failing to distinguish prime parity or target purity.
